messages.subject: blavaan, priors
parts:
Hi all,


I want to use blavaaan, and I was told the following for setting priors.

"For the priors, if you don’t have any prior literature to base them on, you typically set them to 0.5 before running the model."



Could you help me with how to set in blavan? I know that I have to set dpriors but I do not know how I set it.


Thank you

messages.author: 23a4293d4c2373b0
messages.subject: Re: blavaan, priors
parts:
Hi Roxanna, from your question I assume that the variable in question you want to set a prior on must have a binomial distribution.

One important thing to understand is that a "prior" is not a parameter (i.e. a single number, like 0.5 in your case) but a probability distribution. That means that what you refer to as 0.5 probably refers to a parameter that defines the density function of that distribution. In the case of a binomial distribution, where the "typical" (used because of its "conjugate" property) prior is a Beta distribution, 0.5 probably refers to the relationship between the alpha and beta parameters (called "mu" in this response). That would give you a "uniform" (usually understood as "non-informative"*) distribution, but only when alpha = beta = 1. Otherwise, it will give you a symmetric distribution, but the "amount of information" it provides will depend on the actual value of alpha and beta.

I hope this is clear enough, and helpful somehow. In any case, I hate being the one who says it but I think you would need to delve a little deeper into the theory of Bayesian statistical theory to really get an understanding of the topic :)

Daniel

*Please note, terms like "informative" and "information" refer to "how much" previous ("prior") information you want to input into the model, based on your previous assumptions or beliefs, which are based on the prior literature you mention.

--
Daniel Morillo, Ph.D.
